source.title: Adaptive Circuit Behavior and Generalization in Mechanistic Interpretability
source.authors: Jatin Nainani; Sankaran Vaidyanathan; A. Yeung; Kartik Gupta; David Jensen

page_placements.theme: IOI behaviour depends on wording and prompt format

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates the GPT-2 small IOI circuit on new prompt settings using the original circuit and logit-difference measure, and discovers variant circuits with the original path-patching methodology.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on the base IOI circuit, DoubleIO and TripleIO variants, and newly discovered circuits for those variants. Results cited from Wang et al. are not cataloged. The many individual head-level plots are represented here by the explicit aggregate and named-head results described in the text.
record.test_reason: The study uses Wang et al.'s GPT-2 small IOI circuit, logit-difference metric, mean-ablation knockout and path patching. It re-scores the base circuit on base IOI, evaluates it on DoubleIO and TripleIO, and rediscovers circuits for those variants. These results bear on V1 (base faithfulness), V5 (faithfulness depends on prompt distribution and ablation) and V6 (more repeated names, name order).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude the IOI circuit generalizes strongly: it reuses all nodes and paths and adds only edges from the duplicated IO tokens. They say the base circuit's over-performance on the variants (S2 Hacking) is an artifact of mean-ablation knockout. Name order matters, with Previous Token head 2.2 acting as a decision point.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses the original IOI circuit, logit-difference measure, mean-ablation evaluation, and Wang et al.'s path-patching framework. It extends the evaluation to DoubleIO and TripleIO and adds paths to discover variant circuits; it does not re-run the original circuit-discovery study on the original prompt set alone.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt variant changes full-model and circuit scores and faithfulness. In DoubleIO, name order changes performance and head 2.2 attention. Mean ablation creates the S2 Hacking behavior in the evaluated base circuit.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-2 small's own IOI logit difference falls from 3.484 (base) to 2.118 (DoubleIO) to 1.227 (TripleIO) as the IO name is repeated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-model IOI performance degrades when the indirect-object name is duplicated.

record.problems: The paper gives inconsistent DoubleIO full-model logit differences (2.118 in Table 1 and 2.138 in Section 3.2). Figure 2 and Figure 4 contain head-level results that are largely presented graphically; uncertainty intervals are mentioned for Figure 4 based on 50 samples, but no numerical intervals are supplied in the text. Variant datasets contain 200 prompts each.
record.rows_left_out: No reported central result was omitted. The full set of head-by-head confidence-ratio and functional-faithfulness values in Figure 4 and the detailed causal-effect plots in Figures 6, 11-13 are not individually transcribed; the text's explicit named-head findings and aggregate attention-deviation descriptions are represented in r21-r25 and r28.

untested.parts: Completeness and minimality tests; the class-by-class identification of the 26 heads is taken from Wang et al., not redone.
All of it: no ablation of name movers and no measurement of backup heads.
All of it: only GPT-2 small; no other sizes, checkpoints or tasks.
All of it: only path patching with mean ablation; no other methods compared.
Alternative ablation types (resample, zero) and alternative metrics are not compared; mean ablation is only diagnosed as the cause of S2 Hacking.
Other templates beyond the 15 per variant, more than two distinct names, languages and other formats.

missing.what: Confidence ratios and functional faithfulness for heads under S2 Hacking: head 8.6 has a circuit confidence ratio above 2 vs about 1 in the model, with S2 functional faithfulness about 2; heads 3.0, 5.5 and 5.9 behave similarly.
Path patching finds no new name-mover heads and the same S-Inhibition heads as most causal; IO2 and IO3 paths have opposite-sign effects on the Inhibition heads.
Adding paths from input tokens other than the duplicated names leaves performance unchanged (IO1) or degrades it.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1-r3 and r10 are full-model reference values, not tests. The base circuit's high variant scores should not be read as V6 support, since the authors attribute them to an ablation artifact. The V6 support comes from the rediscovered circuits' overlap with the base circuit. The extraction's V5 limits_scope labels are recast as supports, because V5 itself asserts sensitivity of the evaluation.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not re-evaluate whether the base circuit has 26 attention heads in 7 classes or meets the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria on the base IOI task.
Backup name-mover heads taking over after main name-mover ablation are not tested.
Other models, model sizes, training checkpoints, and component reuse across other tasks are not tested.
The study does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics as alternative methods.
The study varies prompt format and reports a mean-ablation artifact, but does not systematically compare ablation types or alternative evaluation metrics.

The study tests base IOI, DoubleIO and TripleIO, and name-order conditions for DoubleIO. It does not establish generalization to arbitrary templates, languages, or other numbers of names beyond these tested variants.

Stored-field errors: r28 swaps 0.56 and 0.57; Figure 8 also resolves r26–r27 numerically. Its subgroup scores are not reconciled with Table 2 aggregates by the source.
Source disagreements: DoubleIO model 2.118 in Tables 1–2 versus 2.138 in Section 3.2; TripleIO normalized faithfulness 0.778 in Table 2 versus 0.79 in Section 5.1. Preserve both with provenance; do not count r19–r20 as independent replications.

statements.correction: Rediscovered circuits: 26 nodes each; node overlap 100%; edge overlap DoubleIO 91.66%, TripleIO 84.61%. Unmodified base circuit on variants: most attention deviations typically within 0.05, Section 3.3.
statements.problem: Node and edge results concern rediscovered circuits, but the cited attention-deviation measurements concern the unmodified base circuit on variant inputs. The conditions conflate these configurations.
For this study, the supported claims are DoubleIO order dependence and the specified head deviations; the preceding systematic BABA/ABBA comparison is not established here.
